notes: Revisión independiente C1 de las clases 56-60: claves verificadas contra textos/audios una a una.
Distractores reescritos como casi-aciertos en 56 p1/e2/e4/r2/r3, 57 e1/e2/e4/r2/r3, 58 p1/p2/r1/r3, 59 p3/r2/r3, 60 p1/e2/e3/r2/r3.
59 p3: ya no hay 'agrees completely'; las opciones difieren en beneficio/inconveniente y en el último acto (pregunta a Tom).
57 e1 ya no revela la clave de e2; 58 p1/p2 y 60 e2 son paráfrasis del audio, no copias literales.

Completar con aceptadas ampliadas (in: join/step/weigh; rephrase: restate/clarify; to a certain point; get/put...). Rúbricas: 59 sin evidencias laxas de 'last week/yesterday'; 60 con grupo de reconducción cortés.
Español neutro: costes→costos, deberes→tareas, Os presento→Les presento, móvil→celular, municipio→municipio.

classes.objetivo: Reconocer quién toma, mantiene, interrumpe o cede el turno en una mesa redonda a partir de las expresiones que usa cada participante.

ensenanza.en: The moderator opened the panel by asking each guest in turn to state one priority for the coming year.
ensenanza.es: La moderadora abrió la mesa pidiendo a cada invitado, por turno, que dijera una prioridad para el año que viene.
ensenanza.nota: In turn indica un orden: uno tras otro, sin que dos hablen a la vez.

ensenanza.en: If I may, I would like to take the floor for a moment, since nobody has yet mentioned the cost.
ensenanza.es: Si me lo permite, me gustaría tomar la palabra un momento, ya que nadie ha mencionado todavía el costo.
ensenanza.nota: Take the floor es pedir o tomar el turno; If I may lo suaviza con cortesía.

ensenanza.en: As I was saying, the cost matters, and I intend to hold the floor until I have finished this point.
ensenanza.es: Como decía, el costo importa, y pienso mantener la palabra hasta terminar este punto.
ensenanza.nota: Hold the floor es retener el turno; As I was saying retoma una idea que alguien acaba de cortar.

ensenanza.en: Sorry to interrupt, but may I chime in here before the discussion moves on?
ensenanza.es: Perdona que interrumpa, pero ¿puedo intervenir ahora, antes de que la discusión avance?
ensenanza.nota: Sorry to interrupt + but pide permiso con cortesía; chime in significa intervenir en una conversación ya empezada.

ensenanza.en: A fair moderator never lets one guest talk over another, and asks the louder guest to yield the floor.
ensenanza.es: Un buen moderador nunca deja que un invitado hable encima de otro, y pide al más ruidoso que ceda la palabra.
ensenanza.nota: Talk over es hablar mientras otro habla; yield the floor es lo que debe hacer quien no respeta el turno.

ensenanza.en: That is all from me; I will hand over to the moderator, and then Leo may go ahead with his reply.
ensenanza.es: Eso es todo por mi parte; cedo la palabra a la moderadora, y después Leo podrá responder.
ensenanza.nota: Hand over to + persona cede el turno; go ahead invita a empezar a quien espera.

explicacion.texto: En una mesa redonda cada frase cumple una función de turno. Tomar la palabra: If I may… / Can I chime in here? Mantenerla: As I was saying… / Let me finish. Interrumpir: Sorry to interrupt, but… Ceder el turno: I will hand over to… / Go ahead… / Over to you. Al escuchar, fíjate en el verbo y en quién habla: el moderador da y cede turnos; los participantes los piden, los mantienen o, si no lo hacen bien, hablan encima del otro. La cortesía se nota en la disculpa breve y en el modal (may, could).

formula.texto: If I may, I would like to add…

formula.nota: ceder el turno a otra persona

filas.texto: If I may… / Can I chime in here?
As I was saying… / Let me finish.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Let me to finish my point.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras let va el verbo en forma base, sin to: let me finish («déjame terminar»).

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I give you the word, Leo.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I give you the floor, Leo.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Dar la palabra» se dice give the floor; the word significa «la palabra» como vocablo, no como turno.

situacion.contexto: Mia modera una mesa redonda sobre tablets en el colegio, con Tom y Sara.

dialogo.texto: Welcome to our panel. Tom, you have the floor.
dialogo.traduccion: Bienvenidos a nuestra mesa redonda. Tom, tienes la palabra.

dialogo.texto: Thank you. Schools must think about cost first, and I intend to hold the floor until I finish this point.
dialogo.traduccion: Gracias. Los colegios deben pensar primero en el costo, y pienso mantener la palabra hasta terminar este punto.

dialogo.texto: Sorry to interrupt, Tom, but may I chime in? I have a number.
dialogo.traduccion: Perdona que te interrumpa, Tom, pero ¿puedo intervenir? Tengo una cifra.

dialogo.texto: Let me finish, Sara. Then I will hand over to you.
dialogo.traduccion: Déjame terminar, Sara. Luego te cedo la palabra.

item.consigna: ¿Cómo reacciona Tom cuando Sara lo interrumpe?

opciones.es: Mantiene su turno y promete cederlo después.
Le cede la palabra enseguida a Sara.
Pide a la moderadora que la interrumpa a ella.

item.feedback: Tom responde «Let me finish» para retener el turno y añade «Then I will hand over to you».

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué función de turno cumple el fragmento?
opciones: She asks politely for a turn to speak.
She keeps a turn that she already holds.
She gives the turn to someone else.
guiada.feedback: «If I may» y «take the floor» piden permiso para empezar a hablar: la oradora solicita el turno.
guiada.texto: If I may, I would like to take the floor for a moment, because nobody has mentioned the people who will pay for all of this.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en quién quiere empezar a hablar y cómo lo pide.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Todos respondieron por turno, sin interrupciones.»
guiada.texto: The moderator looked at the four guests and asked each of them, in turn, for a single priority. Everyone answered ___ turn, without interruptions.
guiada.feedback: In turn significa «uno tras otro»; es la colocación que describe un reparto ordenado del turno.
guiada.pista: Es la preposición de la colocación «___ turn».

guiada.respuesta: Please go ahead, Leo, and tell us what you think
guiada.feedback: Go ahead cede el turno a quien espera, y and tell us invita a continuar con lo que va a decir.
guiada.pista: Empieza con la fórmula que invita a hablar.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hace la moderadora con el turno?
practica.audio: Thank you, Carlos. That was clear, and I think Ana wanted to respond. Ana, the floor is yours, but please keep it brief, because we still have two guests who have not yet spoken.
opciones: She gives the turn to Ana and reminds her of the time.
She gives the turn to Ana and asks her to answer Carlos at length.
She promises Ana more time after the other guests have spoken.
practica.feedback: Agradece a Carlos, cede la palabra a Ana y le recuerda que debe ser breve porque otros esperan.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué hace la oradora ante la interrupción?
opciones: She defends the turn she already holds.
She asks for a turn she does not have.
She hands the turn over to the interrupter.
practica.feedback: «I have not finished» y «As I was saying» defienden el turno propio frente a la interrupción.
practica.texto: Wait, I have not finished. As I was saying, cost is only one part of the problem, and if you let me explain the second part, you will see why it matters more.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con la función que cumple en la mesa.
pares: Can I chime in here for a second?
Please, let me finish this point.
Sorry to interrupt, but I must disagree.
I will hand over to Leo now.
Cede el turno a otra persona
Could we hear from everyone in turn?
practica.feedback: Cada frase tiene su función: entrar, retener, cortar con tacto, ceder u ordenar la palabra.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿por qué no pudo hablar Sara cuando intentó intervenir?
evaluacion.audio: The moderator welcomed the guests and asked each of them in turn for one priority. Tom took the floor first and spoke for nearly three full minutes about cost. Halfway through, Sara tried to add a comment, but Tom carried on, saying that he had not finished. Sara sat back, clearly annoyed, while the rest of the panel waited in silence. When Tom finally handed over, the moderator thanked him, turned to Sara and said: Go ahead, but please keep it brief, because Leo has been waiting patiently for his turn.
opciones: Because Tom refused to yield the floor before finishing.
Because the moderator told her to wait for Leo first.
Because Sara realised that her point was not relevant.
evaluacion.feedback: Tom siguió hablando y dijo que no había terminado: retuvo la palabra y Sara no pudo entrar.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender la última frase de la moderadora?
evaluacion.audio: The moderator welcomed the guests and asked each of them in turn for one priority. Tom took the floor first and spoke for nearly three full minutes about cost. Halfway through, Sara tried to add a comment, but Tom carried on, saying that he had not finished. Sara sat back, clearly annoyed, while the rest of the panel waited in silence. When Tom finally handed over, the moderator thanked him, turned to Sara and said: Go ahead, but please keep it brief, because Leo has been waiting patiently for his turn.
opciones: That she wants to be fair to the guest who spoke least.
That she plans to give Tom a second chance to speak afterwards.
That she hopes the panel will end a little earlier than planned.
evaluacion.feedback: Al pedir brevedad por Leo, que espera desde hace rato, deja ver su interés en repartir la palabra con justicia.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La discusión iba bien hasta que alguien intentó intervenir sin pedir turno.»
evaluacion.texto: The discussion was going well until a guest tried to ___ in without asking, and two people began to talk over each other.
evaluacion.feedback: Chime in es intervenir en una conversación ya iniciada; jump in o cut in son variantes válidas, aunque cut in suena más brusco.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor sobre los moderadores que casi no intervienen?
opciones: They cause problems: the loudest guests end up deciding who speaks.
They are a safe choice, because a silent moderator can never be accused of bias.
They are acceptable only when the guests already know one another.
evaluacion.feedback: Sostiene que la pasividad favorece al más ruidoso y deja sin voz al más prudente: para él moderar es repartir la palabra.
evaluacion.texto: Moderators are often praised for saying little. I disagree. A moderator who never steps in lets the loudest guest decide who speaks, and the quietest guest, who often has the most careful view, leaves without being heard. A good moderator is not silent; the skill lies in asking the right person to take the floor at the right moment.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Nadie debe hablar encima de un colega que todavía está hablando.»
repaso.respuesta: Nobody should talk over a colleague who is still speaking
repaso.feedback: Talk over + persona describe hablar mientras otro habla; who is still speaking explica por qué es una falta de cortesía.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué actitud muestra Sara tras la interrupción?
repaso.audio: Sorry, Tom, I should not have talked over you. You were right to hold the floor, and I will wait for my turn. Having said that, if you would not mind, I have one short figure that may save us some time.
opciones: Apologetic, but still keen to add a short point.
Defensive: she claims that Tom gave her no chance to speak.
Apologetic, but she drops her point entirely to avoid more conflict.
repaso.feedback: Se disculpa y reconoce que Tom tenía derecho a mantener la palabra, pero aun así quiere aportar su cifra con cortesía.

repaso.consigna: ¿Por qué elige la moderadora al estudiante del fondo?
opciones: She gives priority to the person who has waited longest without interrupting.
She prefers him to the other two because his question is better.
She assumes that a student is less likely to ask a difficult question.
repaso.feedback: La espera paciente del estudiante, frente a las otras dos manos levantadas, sugiere que la moderadora premia a quien respeta el turno.
repaso.texto: When the moderator said that there was time for one more question, three hands went up at once. She looked at the back of the room, where a student had been waiting politely for twenty minutes, and said: Yes, you, please go ahead.

classes.objetivo: Interrumpir con cortesía, pedir aclaraciones y reconducir una mesa redonda con fórmulas como Sorry to cut in, If I could just… y Coming back to….

ensenanza.en: Sorry to cut in, but could I clarify one figure before the discussion moves any further?
ensenanza.es: Perdona que te corte, pero ¿podría aclarar una cifra antes de que la discusión avance más?
ensenanza.nota: Sorry to + verbo base (cut in) es la disculpa breve; could I + verbo base pide permiso con suavidad.

ensenanza.en: If I could just rephrase the question, I think it would be easier for every guest to answer.
ensenanza.es: Si pudiera reformular la pregunta, creo que sería más fácil de responder para todos los invitados.
ensenanza.nota: If I could just + verbo pide permiso para hacer algo breve; el modal could lo vuelve cortés.

ensenanza.en: Can I just check that this is directly relevant, or are you about to go off on a tangent?
ensenanza.es: ¿Puedo comprobar si esto es directamente pertinente, o está a punto de irse por las ramas?
ensenanza.nota: Can I just check…? suaviza la duda; go off on a tangent es alejarse del tema principal.

ensenanza.en: Coming back to the budget, could we clarify who pays and pin down the exact figure?
ensenanza.es: Volviendo al presupuesto, ¿podríamos aclarar quién paga y concretar la cifra exacta?
ensenanza.nota: Coming back to + tema reconduce sin reproche; pin down exige una respuesta precisa.

ensenanza.en: To put it another way, a moderator who wants to redirect the debate should do so without blaming anyone.
ensenanza.es: Dicho de otro modo, un moderador que quiera reconducir el debate debe hacerlo sin culpar a nadie.
ensenanza.nota: To put it another way introduce una reformulación; redirect significa dar otra dirección a la conversación.

ensenanza.en: Thank you for that comment; I will take that on board and check the figures again tonight.
ensenanza.es: Gracias por ese comentario; lo tendré en cuenta y revisaré las cifras otra vez esta noche.
ensenanza.nota: Take that on board muestra que aceptas una observación sin ponerte a la defensiva.

explicacion.texto: Tres funciones, tres fórmulas corteses. Interrumpir: Sorry to cut in, but… / If I could just… Pedir aclaración: Can I just check…? / Could you pin down…? / To put it another way… Reconducir: Coming back to… / Is that directly relevant to…? La cortesía sale de una disculpa breve, un modal suave (could, might) y un propósito claro. Tras can o could el verbo va en base, sin to, y cut in no lleva complemento directo. Si te corrigen, responde con take that on board en lugar de justificarte.

formula.texto: but could I clarify one point?
could we pin down who pays?
formula.nota: la pregunta que retoma el hilo

filas.texto: Sorry to cut in, but I have a number.
Can I just check what you mean?
If I could just rephrase that…
Could you pin down the date?

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Sorry for cut in, but I have a question.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Sorry to cut in, but I have a question.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La disculpa breve es Sorry to + verbo base; for + verbo base no existe: tras for iría -ing.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Coming back at the budget, could we clarify who pays?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Coming back to the budget, could we clarify who pays?
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La expresión fija es coming back to + tema; la preposición at es un calco de «volviendo a».

situacion.contexto: Sara modera una mesa y reconduce a Leo, que se ha ido por las ramas.

dialogo.texto: I think schools should buy tablets. My cousin bought a great phone last week, and he loves it.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que los colegios deberían comprar tablets. Mi primo compró un celular estupendo la semana pasada y le encanta.

dialogo.texto: Sorry to cut in, Leo, but is that directly relevant to the budget?
dialogo.traduccion: Perdona que te corte, Leo, pero ¿es eso directamente pertinente para el presupuesto?

dialogo.texto: Good point. I was going off on a tangent.
dialogo.traduccion: Buena observación. Me estaba yendo por las ramas.

dialogo.texto: Coming back to the budget, could you pin down how much the tablets cost?
dialogo.traduccion: Volviendo al presupuesto, ¿podrías concretar cuánto cuestan las tablets?

item.consigna: ¿Qué le pide Sara a Leo al final del diálogo?

opciones.es: Que concrete cuánto cuestan las tablets.
Que explique por qué su primo compró un celular.
Que termine su turno y ceda la palabra.

item.feedback: Sara reconduce con «Coming back to the budget» y le pide «pin down how much the tablets cost».

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Perdona que te corte, pero ¿puedo aclarar una cifra?»
guiada.texto: Two guests were already speaking at once about the figures. Sorry to ___ in, but could I clarify one of them?
guiada.feedback: Sorry to cut in es la disculpa estándar antes de interrumpir; chime in y jump in son variantes válidas.
guiada.pista: Es el verbo que forma con in el verbo compuesto para interrumpir.

opciones: Coming back to the budget, could we settle who pays?
Holidays matter too, so let us leave the budget for another day.
That is an interesting tangent, so let us follow it for a while.
guiada.feedback: Coming back to… vuelve al tema central; las otras dos son amables, pero no reconducen: aplazan el presupuesto o siguen la digresión.
guiada.texto: We were discussing the school budget, but for the last five minutes the conversation has drifted towards summer holidays.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase que devuelve la conversación al tema, no la que la deja seguir.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «¿Podrías precisar la cifra exacta para nosotros?»
guiada.respuesta: Could you pin down the exact figure for us
guiada.feedback: Could you + verbo base forma la petición cortés; pin down pide una respuesta concreta.
guiada.pista: Empieza con la petición cortés Could you.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Si pudiera reformularla, creo que todos la entenderíamos mejor.»
practica.texto: Your question is long, and I am not sure everyone followed it. If I could just ___ it, I think we would all understand it better.
practica.feedback: If I could just + verbo pide permiso para reformular con brevedad; reword y restate son sinónimos válidos.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué intervención pide precisión a Mia con cortesía?
opciones: Could you pin down which of those things matters most?
Would you mind speaking more slowly so that we can follow?
Could we move on, since none of that seems relevant?
practica.feedback: Pide concretar cuál de los factores pesa más, sin reproche; las otras dos son corteses pero piden otra cosa: ritmo o cambiar de tema.
practica.texto: Mia: Well, it depends on the budget, and on a few other things, and on what the parents think, although that is hard to say.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hace el orador con sus primeras palabras?
practica.audio: Sorry to cut in, but that is not quite what I meant. If I could just put it another way, the real issue is not the money but the time that teachers need to learn the new system.
opciones: He politely interrupts to explain his own point again.
He politely interrupts to correct someone's figures.
He politely asks the moderator to change the topic.
practica.feedback: Se disculpa, interrumpe y reformula su propia idea con «put it another way»: corrige un malentendido sobre lo que quiso decir.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hace Leo después de la intervención de Sara?
evaluacion.audio: The debate on school tablets had been calm until Leo began describing his cousin's new phone. Two minutes later he was still talking about its camera. Sara, who was leading the panel, waited for a pause and said: Sorry to cut in, Leo, but is this directly relevant to our budget? Leo laughed and admitted that he had gone off on a tangent. Sara thanked him and continued: Coming back to the budget, could you pin down how much a class set of tablets would cost? Leo said that he would check the figures and take that on board before the next session.
opciones: He admits his digression and agrees to verify the numbers.
He defends his story and insists that the phone matters to the debate.
He asks Sara to give him two more minutes to finish his story.
evaluacion.feedback: Leo se ríe, reconoce que se fue por las ramas y promete comprobar las cifras.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender la pregunta de Sara sobre los comentarios de Leo?
evaluacion.audio: The debate on school tablets had been calm until Leo began describing his cousin's new phone. Two minutes later he was still talking about its camera. Sara, who was leading the panel, waited for a pause and said: Sorry to cut in, Leo, but is this directly relevant to our budget? Leo laughed and admitted that he had gone off on a tangent. Sara thanked him and continued: Coming back to the budget, could you pin down how much a class set of tablets would cost? Leo said that he would check the figures and take that on board before the next session.
opciones: She doubts that they belong to the topic but avoids blaming him.
She believes they are relevant, but wants Leo to state them more briefly.
She suspects that they are meant to delay the discussion on purpose.
evaluacion.feedback: Formula una pregunta en lugar de una orden: deja ver su duda sobre la pertinencia sin culpar a Leo.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa las tres intervenciones: interrumpir, comprobar y reformular.
frases: Sorry to ___ in, but I have a question about the figure.
Can I just ___ that you mean the budget and not the cost of repairs?
If I could just ___ that, I think it would be clearer to the parents.
evaluacion.feedback: Las tres fórmulas corteses llevan verbo base: cut in para interrumpir, check para confirmar y rephrase para reformular.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Cuál es la opinión del autor sobre la reconducción cortés?
opciones: It respects everyone involved, including the guest who drifts.
It is worthwhile only when the moderator knows the guest well.
It is unfair to the guest but necessary for the audience.
evaluacion.feedback: Defiende que reconducir con tacto protege al público, al que está siendo ignorado y hasta al propio invitado que divaga.
evaluacion.texto: Many panel moderators fear the word no. They let a guest drift from the subject because stopping him feels rude. I think the opposite is true. A polite way to redirect the talk, such as coming back to our question, protects the speaker who is being ignored, the audience who came for the topic, and, in the end, the guest who drifted, who would rather be stopped gently than be remembered for rambling.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Volviendo a la pregunta principal, ¿qué decidimos?»
repaso.respuesta: Coming back to the main question, what do we decide
repaso.feedback: Coming back to + tema abre la frase que reconduce, y luego va la pregunta.
aceptadas: What do we decide, coming back to the main question

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué quiere conseguir el orador con su pregunta final?
repaso.audio: Thank you for that comment, Mia. I will take that on board. But may I pin down one thing? When you say soon, do you mean this term or next year?
opciones: A precise date instead of a vague promise.
Confirmation that Mia accepts the criticism she has just heard.
A reason to delay the decision until next year.
repaso.feedback: Pide concretar «soon» entre dos fechas posibles: busca precisión donde ella fue vaga.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender el orador sobre el plan?
opciones: That it may go wrong for the same reason as an earlier one.
That it should be postponed until a cheaper plan is found.
That it is sound and only needs a better budget.
repaso.feedback: No dice que el plan sea malo, pero quiere comprobar que no se repite «the mistake of last year»: insinúa un riesgo conocido.
repaso.texto: I am not saying that the plan is bad. I am saying that nobody has yet explained who will pay for it, and I would like to check that we are not repeating the mistake of last year.

classes.objetivo: Resumir las posturas de otros participantes con verbos de cita precisos (stressed, doubted, warned, insisted, suggested) y colocaciones como concede a point o cast doubt on.

vocabulario.es: admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo

ensenanza.en: Tom stressed that free buses would help poorer families most, but he did not play down the risks.
ensenanza.es: Tom subrayó que los autobuses gratuitos ayudarían sobre todo a las familias más pobres, pero no restó importancia a los riesgos.
ensenanza.nota: Stressed marca lo que el hablante considera esencial; play down es lo contrario: quitar importancia.

ensenanza.en: Sara doubted that the city could afford the scheme, and she cast doubt on the figures in the report.
ensenanza.es: Sara dudó de que la ciudad pudiera permitirse el plan, y puso en duda las cifras del informe.
ensenanza.nota: Doubted that + pasado resume el escepticismo; cast doubt on se aplica al objeto que se cuestiona.

ensenanza.en: Carlos warned that costs could rise, but he was ready to concede a point and to freely admit the idea was good.
ensenanza.es: Carlos advirtió de que los costos podían subir, pero estaba dispuesto a admitir un punto y a reconocer abiertamente que la idea era buena.
ensenanza.nota: Concede a point y freely admit muestran una concesión: el hablante reconoce lo bueno del otro lado.

ensenanza.en: Mia insisted that we must start this year, and she was ready to argue the case for acting at once.
ensenanza.es: Mia insistió en que debíamos empezar este año, y estaba dispuesta a defender la conveniencia de actuar de inmediato.
ensenanza.nota: Insisted that + oración: no lleva preposición (insisted on solo precede a un sustantivo o a un verbo en -ing).

ensenanza.en: Ana suggested that we test it in one district; she was happy to float the idea of a short trial first.
ensenanza.es: Ana sugirió que lo probáramos en un distrito; estaba contenta de lanzar la idea de una prueba breve antes.
ensenanza.nota: Suggested that we + verbo base propone una acción; float the idea la presenta como un globo de ensayo.

ensenanza.en: Some guests were bound to take issue with the plan, so the moderator suggested that they name each objection in turn.
ensenanza.es: Era inevitable que algunos invitados discreparan del plan, así que la moderadora sugirió que nombraran cada objeción por turno.
ensenanza.nota: Take issue with + algo expresa desacuerdo abierto; es más fuerte que disagree.

explicacion.titulo: Resumir lo que dijeron los demás
explicacion.texto: Para resumir una mesa redonda, sustituye said por verbos que muestren la postura de cada persona: stressed (subrayó), doubted (dudó), insisted (insistió), warned (advirtió), suggested (sugirió), o concede a point y freely admit para una concesión. Elige el verbo por la intención, no por cortesía: doubted no es denied. Tras that, la frase suele retroceder un tiempo (can → could, will → would), salvo con modales como must. Al escuchar, pregúntate: ¿defiende, duda, avisa, concede o propone? Y no confundas a quien habla con la persona de la que hablan.

patron.texto: Sujeto + verbo de postura + that + idea:

formula.nota: la idea, con un paso atrás (can → could)

filas.texto: Tom stressed that safety came first.
Sara doubted that it would work.
Carlos warned that prices could rise.
Mia insisted that we must start now.
Ana suggested that we try it first.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Mia insisted in that we start this year.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Mia insisted that we start this year.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Ante that no va preposición; insisted in that es un calco de «insistió en que».

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Ana suggested us to test the idea.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Ana suggested that we test the idea.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Suggest no admite la estructura complemento + to + verbo: se dice suggest that + oración.

situacion.contexto: Ana resume la mesa redonda sobre autobuses gratuitos y Leo comprueba el resumen.

dialogo.texto: Let me recap the panel. Tom stressed that free buses would help poorer families.
dialogo.traduccion: Déjame recapitular la mesa. Tom subrayó que los autobuses gratuitos ayudarían a las familias más pobres.

dialogo.texto: And Sara? I think she doubted that the city could afford them.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y Sara? Creo que dudó de que la ciudad pudiera permitírselos.

dialogo.texto: Right. Carlos warned that costs could rise, but he was ready to concede a point: the idea was good.
dialogo.traduccion: Correcto. Carlos advirtió de que los costos podían subir, pero estaba dispuesto a admitir un punto: la idea era buena.

dialogo.texto: So it is a good idea with some risks, and Mia insisted that we must start this year.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces es una buena idea con algunos riesgos, y Mia insistió en que debemos empezar este año.

opciones.es: Advirtió de que los costos podían subir y reconoció que la idea era buena.
Dudó de que la ciudad pudiera pagar los autobuses.
Insistió en que debían empezar este año.

item.feedback: Ana dice que Carlos «warned that costs could rise» y estaba dispuesto a «concede a point»; dudar fue Sara e insistir, Mia.

guiada.consigna: Elige el resumen fiel de lo que dijo Leo.
opciones: Leo conceded that the plan was not perfect.
Leo doubted that the plan deserved a trial.
Leo suggested that the plan be dropped at once.
guiada.feedback: «You are right» y «the plan is not perfect» muestran una concesión abierta: conceded resume ese reconocimiento.
guiada.texto: Leo: You are right, the plan is not perfect, and I will say so openly, but I still think it deserves our support.
guiada.pista: Leo reconoce algo incómodo, pero mantiene su apoyo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Carlos advirtió de que los costos podían duplicarse.»
guiada.texto: Carlos ___ that costs could double within two years, so he urged the panel to plan carefully.
guiada.feedback: Warned that + riesgo futuro resume un aviso; cautioned es un sinónimo más formal.
guiada.pista: Es el verbo que resume un aviso sobre un peligro futuro.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Tom se negó a quitar importancia a los riesgos del plan.»
guiada.respuesta: Tom refused to play down the risks of the plan
guiada.feedback: Refused to + verbo base expresa rechazo; play down es quitar importancia, y aquí se niega.
guiada.pista: El sujeto es Tom y el verbo de rechazo va después.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿cómo resumirías lo que dijo Carlos?
practica.audio: If we do not plan carefully, costs could double within two years, and the families who already struggle will be the ones who pay for it.
opciones: He warned that careless planning could make the bill twice as high.
He admitted that the bill had already doubled for some families.
He doubted that careful planning would change what families pay.
practica.feedback: El aviso de un riesgo futuro (la factura podría duplicarse) se resume con warned.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿cómo resumirías la postura de la oradora?
practica.audio: I will not accept a later date. We have waited long enough, and if the council will not start this year, I will keep asking until it does.
opciones: She insisted that the work begin before the year ends.
She suggested that the work might begin within the year.
She conceded that the work could wait another year.
practica.feedback: Rechaza otra fecha y mantiene su exigencia con firmeza: insisted, no suggested ni admitted.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que hace el hablante.
pares: float the idea of a trial
Lanzar una propuesta para ver cómo reaccionan
Admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo
practica.feedback: Cada colocación matiza la postura: restar importancia, dudar, proponer, discrepar o conceder.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿quién puso en duda la encuesta de la biblioteca?
evaluacion.audio: Four guests discussed whether the town library should open on Sundays. Luna stressed that working families have no other free day, and she refused to play down the benefits. Rex doubted that the council could pay for extra staff, and he took issue with the survey that the library had published. Sol freely admitted that Sundays were expensive, but she insisted that books were a public service. The moderator then floated the idea of a six-month trial, and all four guests said that they could live with that, provided the results were published.
opciones: Rex, who doubted that the council could pay for extra staff.
Luna, who refused to play down the benefits of opening on Sundays.
Sol, who admitted that Sundays would cost the council a great deal.
evaluacion.feedback: Fue Rex quien «took issue with the survey»; Luna subrayó los beneficios y Sol admitió el costo.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué se puede deducir de la posición final de los invitados?
evaluacion.audio: Four guests discussed whether the town library should open on Sundays. Luna stressed that working families have no other free day, and she refused to play down the benefits. Rex doubted that the council could pay for extra staff, and he took issue with the survey that the library had published. Sol freely admitted that Sundays were expensive, but she insisted that books were a public service. The moderator then floated the idea of a six-month trial, and all four guests said that they could live with that, provided the results were published.
opciones: That they would accept a trial if its results were made public.
That they had finally settled their disagreement about the cost of opening.
That they all wanted the library to open every single Sunday without delay.
evaluacion.feedback: Aceptan la prueba «provided the results were published»: una aceptación condicionada, no un acuerdo sobre el costo.

evaluacion.consigna: Relaciona cada frase directa con el verbo que la resume.
pares: Watch out: if we rush, the costs will climb.
I really doubt that the budget can cover this.
Fair enough, you have a point there.
We will not move until the date is fixed.
Perhaps we could try it in one school first.
evaluacion.feedback: El verbo de cita se elige por la intención: aviso, duda, concesión, insistencia o propuesta.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Sara solo puso en duda las cifras en que se basaba el informe.»
evaluacion.texto: Sara did not say that the plan was useless. She only ___ doubt on the figures that the report was based on.
evaluacion.feedback: Cast doubt on es la colocación habitual; throw doubt on y shed doubt on son variantes menos frecuentes.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué reprocha el autor al acta de la reunión?
opciones: That a neutral verb hides the real differences between the guests.
That it was written by someone who missed most of the meeting.
That it gives too much space to the most critical guest.
repaso.feedback: Critica que «discussed» oculte quién defendió, quién dudó y quién insistió: un verbo neutro borra las posturas.
repaso.texto: After two hours, the chair's report said that the guests discussed the plan. Anyone who was in the room knows that two guests argued the case for it, one doubted it, and one insisted on a different plan from the start. The word discussed hides all of this.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Leo defendió que la prueba durara un año completo.»
repaso.respuesta: Leo argued that the trial should run for a full year
repaso.feedback: Argued that + oración resume una postura defendida con razones; should run expresa lo que propone.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué da a entender el orador sobre el plan?
repaso.audio: They said that the plan was fine, and on paper it is. But I notice that nobody has said who will answer the phone at midnight when it goes wrong.
opciones: That it has a practical weakness nobody has addressed.
That it is too difficult for ordinary users to follow.
That its authors are hiding the real cost.
repaso.feedback: Reconoce que sobre el papel funciona, pero señala que nadie ha resuelto qué pasa cuando falla: una debilidad práctica.

classes.objetivo: Aportar una opinión concordando parcialmente, ampliar lo dicho por otro con un ejemplo y devolver el turno con una pregunta a otro participante.

vocabulario.es: entiendo lo que dices, tienes razón en eso
hasta cierto punto, en cierta medida

ensenanza.en: I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback: a ban would treat the symptom and ignore the cause.
ensenanza.es: Estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto, pero veo un inconveniente: una prohibición trataría el síntoma e ignoraría la causa.
ensenanza.nota: Up to a point limita el acuerdo; después de but aparece el matiz (aquí, un drawback).

ensenanza.en: I take your point, and it is a valid point, although I partly disagree with the conclusion you draw from it.
ensenanza.es: Entiendo lo que dices, y es un punto válido, aunque discrepo en parte de la conclusión que sacas de él.
ensenanza.nota: I take your point reconoce la idea del otro sin aceptar su conclusión; partly suaviza el desacuerdo.

ensenanza.en: Building on what my fellow participant said, I would go further and, for instance, give every school a clear rule.
ensenanza.es: Partiendo de lo que dijo mi compañero de mesa, yo iría más lejos y, por ejemplo, daría a cada colegio una norma clara.
ensenanza.nota: Building on + lo dicho amplía; I would go further anuncia que llevas la idea más allá que el otro.

ensenanza.en: For instance, in my school, tablets saved hours of copying, yet few pupils read more as a result.
ensenanza.es: Por ejemplo, en mi colegio las tablets ahorraron horas de copia, pero pocos alumnos leyeron más como resultado.
ensenanza.nota: For instance + coma introduce un caso concreto; yet añade un matiz que limita el ejemplo.

ensenanza.en: Furthermore, the idea works best when parents help, and I would like to flesh out that point briefly.
ensenanza.es: Además, la idea funciona mejor cuando los padres ayudan, y me gustaría desarrollar ese punto brevemente.
ensenanza.nota: Furthermore suma un argumento; flesh out + punto anuncia que vas a desarrollarlo con más detalle.

ensenanza.en: To a certain extent the trial worked, but its main drawback was the extra time that teachers needed to prepare.
ensenanza.es: Hasta cierto punto la prueba funcionó, pero su principal inconveniente fue el tiempo extra que los profesores necesitaron para prepararse.
ensenanza.nota: To a certain extent es sinónimo de up to a point; se usa igual para acotar un acuerdo o un éxito.

explicacion.titulo: Construir sobre la idea de otro
explicacion.texto: Un buen acuerdo parcial reconoce lo válido y después matiza: I take your point… / I agree up to a point, but… / That is a valid point; however… Luego amplías con Building on that… o Furthermore… y respaldas con For instance,… Por último, devuelves el turno con una pregunta dirigida a otro participante: Mia, what have you noticed? Así la mesa avanza en lugar de acumular opiniones sueltas. Recuerda: agree es un verbo, no un adjetivo, y partly va delante del verbo (I partly agree).

formula.nota: devuelves el turno con una pregunta

filas.texto: I agree up to a point / I partly agree
Building on that, we could test it.
For instance, my class saved paper.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am partly agree with you.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo, no un adjetivo como «de acuerdo»: no lleva am.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Building in what Mia said, I would add a reason.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Building on what Mia said, I would add a reason.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: La expresión es build on («partir de», «apoyarse en»), con la preposición on.

situacion.contexto: Ana y Carlos debaten sobre las tablets en clase y se apoyan en lo que dice el otro.

dialogo.texto: Tablets help students, and they save paper.
dialogo.traduccion: Las tablets ayudan a los estudiantes y ahorran papel.

dialogo.texto: I take your point, Ana, and I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback: screens can distract.
dialogo.traduccion: Entiendo lo que dices, Ana, y estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto, pero veo un inconveniente: las pantallas pueden distraer.

dialogo.texto: That is a valid point. For instance, my brother stops reading when a message arrives.
dialogo.traduccion: Es un punto válido. Por ejemplo, mi hermano deja de leer cuando llega un mensaje.

dialogo.texto: Building on that, Ana, what do you do to avoid it?
dialogo.traduccion: Partiendo de eso, Ana, ¿qué haces tú para evitarlo?

opciones.es: Que las pantallas pueden distraer a los alumnos.
Que el papel resulta demasiado caro.
Que los alumnos no tienen tablets.

item.feedback: Carlos concede parte de la idea de Ana y señala el inconveniente: «screens can distract».

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Veo un inconveniente: castigaría a quienes usan el celular para aprender.»
guiada.texto: I accept that a complete ban would make things easier, but I see one ___: it would hurt the students who use phones to learn.
guiada.feedback: Drawback es el inconveniente que matiza un acuerdo parcial; downside y disadvantage son sinónimos válidos.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo que nombra el punto débil de una idea.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Entiendo tu punto, pero discrepo en parte.»
guiada.respuesta: I take your point, but I partly disagree
guiada.feedback: I take your point reconoce la idea y but partly disagree matiza el desacuerdo.
guiada.pista: Empieza con la fórmula que reconoce la idea del otro.

opciones: I agree up to a point, but I see one drawback for some learners.
I agree completely, Leo, and I can see no drawback at all in a ban.
I disagree entirely, Leo, because phones are useful in every class.
guiada.feedback: Up to a point y un drawback dejan ver un acuerdo con reservas; las otras respuestas aceptan o rechazan del todo.
guiada.texto: Leo: Schools should ban phones completely.
guiada.pista: El acuerdo parcial acepta algo y luego matiza.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Partiendo de su idea, añadiría que casi no cuestan nada.»
practica.texto: Mia made a good case for more outdoor lessons. ___ on her idea, I would add that they cost almost nothing.
practica.feedback: Building on + idea ajena es la fórmula para ampliar; expanding on funciona igual.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué intervención amplía la idea de Mia en lugar de repetirla?
opciones: Building on that, phones could stay in a box during lessons and come out at break.
I agree with Mia: screens distract children in class, and that is a serious problem for teachers.
Mia is wrong: screens distract children far less than noise does in most rooms.
practica.feedback: Añade una propuesta nueva que parte de lo dicho; las otras repiten la idea o la rechazan.
practica.texto: Mia: Screens distract children in class, especially when a message arrives in the middle of an explanation.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿cómo interviene la oradora en el debate?
practica.audio: I can see what you mean, and to a certain extent I agree. Tablets made our lessons tidier. For instance, nobody lost a worksheet all term. But did reading improve? Tom, you teach the older group: what did you notice?
opciones: She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then asks Tom what he has seen.
She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then asks Tom to prove that it is real.
She accepts part of the idea, gives a benefit and then answers her own question about reading.
practica.feedback: Acepta parte de la idea, aporta un beneficio (la hoja que nadie perdió) y termina preguntando a Tom qué ha observado.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tu intervención: acuerdo parcial, ampliación con ejemplo y una pregunta.
evaluacion.texto: Mesa redonda sobre libros y tablets. Leo dijo: «Los colegios deberían sustituir los libros de papel por tablets». Responde en inglés (150–230 palabras): reconoce lo válido de su idea, expresa un acuerdo parcial (up to a point, partly), amplía con un ejemplo (for instance) y termina con una pregunta dirigida a otra participante, Mia.
evaluacion.respuesta: Thank you, Leo. I take your point, and I agree with you up to a point. Tablets are light, they are cheap to update, and a child can carry a whole library in one bag. But I see one drawback in a complete switch: many pupils read more slowly on a screen, and they get distracted by notifications. For instance, last month my teacher asked us to read a short story on a tablet, and half of the class ended up checking messages. Building on your idea, I would suggest a simple compromise: tablets for research and exercises, and paper for long reading. Furthermore, we could ask pupils to help us write the rules, because people follow what they choose. That is partly why I would not remove paper completely. Mia, what have you noticed with the younger children you work with? Do they read better on paper or on a screen? I would like to hear your view before we decide anything.
aceptadas: Thanks, Leo. That is a fair point, and to a certain extent I agree with you, because tablets really do save a lot of weight and money. However, I see one problem: a screen makes it easy to open something else. For example, yesterday I tried to read a chapter on my tablet and I answered four messages before the end of the first page. Expanding on your idea, I would like to propose that every school keeps a set of paper books for long reading, and uses tablets for everything else. I would add that pupils should choose the books themselves, because a child reads more when the book belongs to them. Mia, what is your experience with the youngest pupils? Would the same plan work for them, or do they need something different? I am curious about your view, and I would like to hear it before we make any decision.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena intervención reconoce lo válido, matiza el acuerdo, amplía con un ejemplo y devuelve el turno con una pregunta a Mia.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hace la oradora con la idea de Leo?
evaluacion.audio: Homework builds habits, and I agree with Leo up to a point. But for some pupils it only adds stress, and I have seen that with my own eyes. Take the case of my neighbour's son: he finishes his homework at ten at night and then cannot sleep. Furthermore, the teachers who set the most homework rarely have time to mark it properly, so the effort often disappears without a word of feedback. So I would not remove homework completely; I would reduce it, and I would make sure that every task counts for something.
opciones: She accepts part of the idea but adds a problem.
She accepts the whole idea and adds an example to support it.
She accepts part of the idea and then asks Leo for evidence.
evaluacion.feedback: «Up to a point» limita su acuerdo con Leo, y el «But» introduce el problema: el estrés de algunos alumnos.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender sobre los profesores que mandan más tareas?
evaluacion.audio: Homework builds habits, and I agree with Leo up to a point. But for some pupils it only adds stress, and I have seen that with my own eyes. Take the case of my neighbour's son: he finishes his homework at ten at night and then cannot sleep. Furthermore, the teachers who set the most homework rarely have time to mark it properly, so the effort often disappears without a word of feedback. So I would not remove homework completely; I would reduce it, and I would make sure that every task counts for something.
opciones: That they may not give it the attention it deserves.
That they do not believe that it builds good habits.
That they are unaware of the stress that it causes.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice que rara vez tienen tiempo de corregirlos bien: sugiere que las tareas reciben menos atención de la debida.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La prueba fue un éxito hasta cierto punto; los alumnos aún necesitaban ayuda.»
evaluacion.texto: The results were encouraging, and the trial was a success to a certain ___; however, most pupils still needed a lot of help.
evaluacion.feedback: To a certain extent (o degree) limita el éxito: funcionó, pero no del todo.

repaso.consigna: Reescribe con acuerdo parcial: Tom tiene razón, pero su idea tiene un problema.
repaso.texto: Tom is right, but his idea has a problem.
repaso.respuesta: Tom is right up to a point, but his idea has a drawback.
aceptadas: I partly agree with Tom, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is partly right, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is right to a certain extent, but his idea has a drawback.
I agree with Tom to a certain extent, but his idea has a drawback.
Tom is partly right, but his idea has a problem.
repaso.feedback: Up to a point o partly convierten un acuerdo total en parcial, y drawback nombra el problema con precisión.

repaso.consigna: ¿Cuál es la idea principal del autor?
opciones: That good panels depend on guests who respond to one another.
That panels improve when guests prepare their speeches more carefully.
That races between panellists make a discussion more exciting to follow.
repaso.feedback: Contrasta los discursos preparados con el intercambio real: lo que da forma a una mesa es responder a lo que dijo el otro.
repaso.texto: Some participants treat a panel like a race: each one waits for a gap, then delivers a prepared speech that ignores what came before. The best panels feel different. Someone says I take your point, but, and suddenly the conversation has a shape.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué hace la moderadora al final?
repaso.audio: That was a valid point, Sara, and it leads me to one question. Carlos, you have run the trial for a full term: did pupils read more, or only faster?
opciones: She acknowledges Sara and asks Carlos a precise question about the trial.
She disputes Sara's point and asks Carlos to answer it on her behalf.
She thanks Carlos for the trial and asks the audience for questions.
repaso.feedback: Reconoce el punto de Sara y pasa el turno a Carlos con una pregunta precisa sobre su experiencia.

classes.objetivo: Moderar una mesa redonda de tres voces: dar la bienvenida, presentar el tema, ceder turnos, reconducir con cortesía, resumir las posturas y cerrar agradeciendo.

vocabulario.es: hilar las ideas, resumir en conjunto
abrir el turno de preguntas al público

ensenanza.en: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone and introduce tonight's topic: how technology is changing the classroom.
ensenanza.es: Permítanme dar una cálida bienvenida a todos y presentar el tema de esta noche: cómo la tecnología está cambiando el aula.
ensenanza.nota: Extend a warm welcome es la fórmula formal de apertura; introduce sirve tanto para personas como para temas.

ensenanza.en: Before we begin, I will set the agenda: a quick round of views, one question from the floor, and a closing summary.
ensenanza.es: Antes de empezar, fijaré el orden del día: una ronda rápida de opiniones, una pregunta del público y un resumen final.
ensenanza.nota: Set the agenda anuncia la estructura de la sesión, igual que una señal de organización en una charla.

ensenanza.en: Each panellist will weigh the benefits against the risks, and I will keep the discussion on track if anyone drifts.
ensenanza.es: Cada ponente sopesará las ventajas frente a los riesgos, y yo mantendré la discusión encauzada si alguien se desvía.
ensenanza.nota: Weigh the benefits + against indica comparación; keep the discussion on track es la tarea central del moderador.

ensenanza.en: Let me draw the threads together: our first panellist stressed the gains, and our second cast doubt on the cost.
ensenanza.es: Déjenme hilar las ideas: nuestro primer ponente subrayó las ventajas y el segundo puso en duda el costo.
ensenanza.nota: Draw the threads together resume posturas distintas con verbos variados (stressed, cast doubt on).

ensenanza.en: Once every panellist has spoken, I will open the floor to questions and then wrap up the session on time.
ensenanza.es: Cuando cada ponente haya hablado, abriré el turno de preguntas y después cerraré la sesión a tiempo.
ensenanza.nota: Open the floor to questions da la palabra al público; wrap up the session es la señal de cierre.

ensenanza.en: To close this round of discussions, I am deeply grateful to each guest for a lively, honest and generous exchange.
ensenanza.es: Para cerrar esta ronda de debates, estoy profundamente agradecido a cada invitado por un intercambio animado, sincero y generoso.
ensenanza.nota: Deeply grateful to + persona dirige el agradecimiento; of sería un calco de «agradecido de».

explicacion.texto: Moderar es estructurar, no opinar. Empieza con una bienvenida y presenta el tema y a los ponentes (Let me introduce…), y fija el orden del día. Reparte los turnos con claridad (Ana, would you like to start? Tom, your turn) y, si alguien se desvía, reconduce con cortesía (Sorry to cut in, but coming back to…). Antes de cerrar, hila las ideas con verbos variados (Ana stressed…, Tom doubted…) y termina agradeciendo (To wrap up…; I am deeply grateful to…). Un buen moderador habla poco y deja que los ponentes se oigan entre sí.

formula.nota: presentas la mesa y el tema

formula.texto: Ana, would you like to start?
Let me draw the threads together:
To wrap up, I am deeply grateful to…

filas.texto: Ana, would you like to start?
To wrap up, I am deeply grateful to…

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Les presento a…» no se dice present you: para presentar personas se usa introduce, y present lleva to.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: To wrap up, I am grateful of all the panellists.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: To wrap up, I am grateful to all the panellists.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras grateful la preposición es to + persona; of es un calco del español «agradecido de».

situacion.contexto: Mia modera una mesa redonda con Ana y Tom sobre tecnología en el aula.

dialogo.texto: I extend a warm welcome to everyone. Tonight's topic is technology in the classroom, and I will set the agenda: a round of views, then questions.
dialogo.traduccion: Doy una cálida bienvenida a todos. El tema de esta noche es la tecnología en el aula, y fijaré el orden del día: una ronda de opiniones y luego preguntas.

dialogo.texto: Thank you. Tablets have clear benefits, but they need rules.
dialogo.traduccion: Gracias. Las tablets tienen ventajas claras, pero necesitan normas.

dialogo.texto: I agree up to a point. Screens can distract students, so we need clear rules.
dialogo.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo hasta cierto punto. Las pantallas pueden distraer a los estudiantes, así que necesitamos normas claras.

dialogo.texto: Let me draw the threads together: both of you stressed rules. I am deeply grateful to you both.
dialogo.traduccion: Déjenme hilar las ideas: los dos subrayaron las normas. Les estoy profundamente agradecida a ambos.

item.consigna: ¿En qué coinciden los dos ponentes, según Mia?

opciones.es: En que hacen falta normas para las pantallas.
En que hay que prohibir las tablets.
En que las tablets no tienen ventajas.

item.feedback: Mia resume: «both of you stressed rules»; Ana y Tom coinciden en la necesidad de normas.

guiada.consigna: Elige la apertura adecuada de una moderadora que presenta la mesa.
opciones: Welcome, everyone; tonight's topic is homework, and I will set the agenda in a moment.
Hello. I will now give my own opinion on homework, and then you may comment.
Good evening. Please be quiet while I explain why homework is useless.
guiada.feedback: Dar la bienvenida, anunciar el tema y fijar el orden del día es lo propio de quien modera; las otras opciones imponen su opinión.
guiada.pista: La moderadora da la bienvenida y presenta el tema, no su opinión.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Déjame presentar a Sara, nuestra primera ponente.»
guiada.texto: Let me ___ Sara, our first panellist, who has taught science for twenty years.
guiada.feedback: Introduce es el verbo habitual para presentar a una persona ante un grupo.
guiada.pista: No es present: es el verbo para presentar a personas.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Empecemos con una ronda breve de opiniones.»
guiada.respuesta: Let us begin with a short round of views
guiada.feedback: Let us begin with… abre la dinámica y a short round of views fija el formato de la sesión.

practica.consigna: Escucha: ¿cómo cede el turno la moderadora?
practica.audio: Thank you, Ana. Tom, I know you see this slightly differently. Please go ahead, but keep in mind that Sara is also waiting, so let us try to stay within three minutes each.
opciones: She gives the turn to Tom and reminds him of the time.
She gives the turn to Tom and promises Sara an extra minute later.
She gives the turn to Tom and asks him to respond to Sara.
practica.feedback: Agradece a Ana, cede la palabra a Tom y le recuerda el límite de tres minutos porque Sara también espera.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué resumen de la moderadora es fiel a ambas posturas?
opciones: Ana stressed the time saved, while Tom doubted that schools could pay for them.
Ana stressed the time saved, while Tom warned that schools would waste money on them.
Ana suggested buying more tablets, while Tom doubted that they saved time.
practica.feedback: Ana subraya el ahorro de tiempo y Tom duda de que los colegios puedan pagarlas; las otras versiones deforman una de las dos posturas.
practica.texto: Ana said that tablets saved time in her classes. Tom replied that he doubted that schools could afford enough of them.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con el momento de la mesa.
pares: Let me extend a warm welcome to everyone.
Let me draw the threads together.
I will open the floor to questions now.
I am deeply grateful to each of you.
practica.feedback: Cada frase marca una etapa de la mesa: abrir, dar turno, resumir, abrir preguntas o cerrar.

evaluacion.consigna: Modera la mesa: presenta, da dos turnos, resume y cierra.
evaluacion.texto: Mesa redonda de tres voces sobre tecnología en el aula (Ana a favor, Tom con dudas sobre el costo, Sara pide normas). Escribe en inglés lo que dirías como moderadora (170–250 palabras): da la bienvenida y presenta el tema y a los ponentes; cede dos turnos; reconduce con cortesía; resume cada postura con verbos variados (stressed, doubted, suggested…); y cierra agradeciendo.
evaluacion.respuesta: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to tonight's panel. Our topic is technology in the classroom. Let me introduce our three panellists: Ana, who uses tablets every day; Tom, who teaches science; and Sara, who has three children at school. Ana, would you like to start? Thank you, Ana. Tom, it is your turn. Sorry to cut in, Tom, but coming back to the main question, could you pin down the cost? Thank you. Before we move on, let me draw the threads together. Ana stressed that tablets saved time. Tom doubted that schools could afford them, and he warned that screens could distract pupils. Sara suggested that we write clear rules, and she conceded that tablets had real benefits. Sara, what would your first rule be? Seldom have I seen three guests agree on so much. To wrap up, all of you agree that rules matter more than machines. I am deeply grateful to each panellist for a lively discussion, and I thank our audience for listening. Good night, everyone.
aceptadas: Welcome, everyone, to our panel. Tonight's topic is technology in the school, and I would like to introduce Ana, Tom and Sara. Ana, please start us off. Thank you. Tom, over to you. Coming back to the topic, could you explain the cost of a class set? Thank you, Tom. Let me recap what we have heard. Ana stressed that tablets saved time. Tom doubted that schools could pay for them. Sara suggested that we make clear rules, and she admitted that tablets helped her own pupils. Is that a fair summary? Good. Sara, what would your first rule be? Sorry to cut in, Tom, but I think that Sara wants to add one short point about homework. Sara, please go ahead. To sum up, everybody agrees that rules matter. I am grateful to each panellist for this lively discussion. Good night, and thank you all for listening. It was a real pleasure to lead this discussion.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena moderación presenta, cede turnos, reconduce, resume con verbos precisos y cierra agradeciendo.

evidencias: i would like to hear from

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué condición pone Tom para apoyar las tablets?
evaluacion.audio: Near the end of the panel, the moderator summed up: Ana stressed that tablets save time, Tom doubted that schools can afford them, and Sara suggested writing clear rules. Then she asked whether that was a fair summary. Tom nodded, but added that he would support tablets if the council published the real costs. Ana said that she could live with that, and Sara reminded everyone that rules cost nothing. The moderator smiled, thanked all three, and said that, for once, a panel on technology had ended with a plan instead of a quarrel.
opciones: That the authorities make the true figures public.
That schools limit them to a few classrooms.
That the pupils help to write the rules.
evaluacion.feedback: Tom asintió al resumen, pero añadió que las apoyaría si el municipio publicara los costos reales.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender el comentario final de la moderadora?
evaluacion.audio: Near the end of the panel, the moderator summed up: Ana stressed that tablets save time, Tom doubted that schools can afford them, and Sara suggested writing clear rules. Then she asked whether that was a fair summary. Tom nodded, but added that he would support tablets if the council published the real costs. Ana said that she could live with that, and Sara reminded everyone that rules cost nothing. The moderator smiled, thanked all three, and said that, for once, a panel on technology had ended with a plan instead of a quarrel.
opciones: That this panel achieved more than such panels usually do.
That panels on technology are usually too short to matter.
That the guests avoided discussing their real disagreements.
evaluacion.feedback: «For once» sugiere que lo habitual es terminar en disputa: valora que esta mesa acabara con un plan.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Su tarea era mantener la discusión encauzada y ser justa con todos.»
evaluacion.texto: The moderator did not give her own opinion. Her job was to ___ the discussion on track and to give every panellist a fair hearing.
evaluacion.feedback: Keep the discussion on track es la colocación que describe la tarea central de quien modera.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Estoy profundamente agradecido a cada ponente por la discusión de esta noche.»
repaso.respuesta: I am deeply grateful to each panellist for tonight's discussion
repaso.feedback: Deeply grateful to + persona dirige el agradecimiento, y for + sustantivo indica el motivo.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre los resúmenes descuidados?
opciones: That they may soften a guest's position to please the room.
That they tend to give too much time to the guest who spoke last.
That guests rarely notice any real difference between the two versions.
repaso.feedback: Advierte que un resumen debe ser fiel aunque incomode: sugiere que el descuido tiende a suavizar la postura de alguien para agradar.
repaso.texto: A summary is not a vote. When a moderator draws the threads together, she must not choose the most comfortable version of what each guest said. If Sara doubted the plan, the summary says that she doubted it, even if the room would prefer to hear that she had merely asked a question.

repaso.consigna: Escucha: ¿qué valora más la moderadora al cerrar?
repaso.audio: Our time is up. Thank you for coming, and thank you most of all to our panellists, who disagreed with great courtesy, which is rarer than people think.
opciones: The polite way in which the guests disagreed.
The passion with which the guests defended their views.
The number of people who came to the session.
repaso.feedback: Da las gracias sobre todo a los ponentes «who disagreed with great courtesy»: valora la cortesía en el desacuerdo.
